fieldMarks: Very large, densely furred, snowshoe-like feet, at least twice the size of a bobcat's.
Short tail with a tip that is completely black all the way around.
Long hind legs give a stooped look with the hind end slightly raised.
Winter coat light grey and faintly spotted; summer coat shorter and reddish-brown.
behavior: Solitary apart from breeding pairs and females with kittens, which sometimes hunt hares together in a line.
Hunts mainly at night, stalking or waiting in ambush.
Specialist predator of snowshoe hare, which can exceed 75% of the diet; lynx numbers cycle with hares roughly every 10 years.
Breeding season late February through March.
habitat: Boreal forest with deep snow, especially young, dense spruce-fir that supports snowshoe hares; also mature forest with dense undergrowth, rocky areas and tundra.
range: Common throughout the boreal forests of Alaska and Canada. In the contiguous United States, resident breeding populations are mainly in Maine, Minnesota, Montana and Washington, with a reintroduced population in Colorado and small numbers in northern New Hampshire and Vermont.

lookalikes.name: Bobcat
lookalikes.howToTell: The bobcat has short ear tufts, smaller feet, a flatter back, more distinct spots, and a tail tip black only on top with white underneath.
